Risk: Sensor destroyed or swept away in extreme flow
Mitigation: Non-contact ultrasonic/radar sensors mounted above historical maximum flood line; replacement budgeted as a consumable, not capex

Risk: Cellular signal lost during the storm, when it matters most
Mitigation: Dual uplink - LoRaWAN mesh between sensors as primary, cellular as backup

Risk: Monsoon cloud cover blocks optical satellite imagery
Mitigation: Sentinel-1 SAR imagery penetrates cloud; primary feed during active monsoon

Risk: Satellite revisit too slow to catch fast lahar shifts after one storm
Mitigation: Drone flyover auto-triggered when a PULSE sensor crosses its warning threshold

Risk: Alert fatigue erodes trust after false alarms
Mitigation: Three-tier language - Watch / Warning / Evacuate Now - instead of binary alerting

Risk: Power or cell outage cuts off the highest-risk households
Mitigation: Solar-charged barangay siren/beacon on the same PULSE threshold; no phone required
Status older than 2 hours auto-downgrades to 'Unconfirmed - proceed with caution'
Only barangay-verified officer accounts can set status; residents may flag for review

Risk: Lahar-sand revenue fluctuates with construction demand
Mitigation: Reserve-fund structure - bank surplus in high-demand quarters against low ones

Risk: LGU turnover ends political sponsorship mid-rollout
Mitigation: MOU at provincial PDRRMO level, not city administration alone; data stays with the LGU
